Senate.job: The winner is one of 100 votes on federal law, spending, treaties, and judges. The term is six years. The U.S. Senate has the sole power to conduct impeachment trials.

scott colom.bio: His campaign says he is a seventh-generation Mississippian from Columbus, a husband and father of two, and that he has been a prosecutor, a judge, and a district attorney. He says he is running for the Senate to put Mississippi first.
issues: He says he would vote to take back Congress's power over tariffs and to require a vote of Congress before the country goes to war.
He says a full day's work should pay enough to build a life in the community where the job is.
He says he would seek a seat on the Agriculture Committee so farmers have a senator answering to them.

ty pinkins.role: Attorney and independent candidate for U.S. Senate.
ty pinkins.bio: His campaign says he grew up in Rolling Fork, the son of a tractor driver, chopped cotton as a teenager, and was the first in his family to finish high school and attend college. He says he is running as an independent because he believes neither party is listening.
issues: He says health care is a right and that he supports the Medicare for All Act.
He says he is not tied to either party or to lobbyists who profit from the current insurance system.
He says his own father's untreated diabetes, and the loss of work and a vehicle that followed, is why the issue is personal.

cindy hyde-smith.role: U.S. senator from Mississippi seeking another term.
cindy hyde-smith.bio: She says rumors that she would not run again are false and that she is definitely planning to campaign for reelection. She says the campaign is a grassroots fight for conservative leadership for Mississippi.
issues: Her campaign issues page highlights Second Amendment rights and balancing the budget.
It also highlights health care and defending unborn life.
It lists stopping illegal immigration and supporting the military and veterans.

bennie thompson.bio: His campaign says he has a long record of bringing federal funding home, and that in 2024 and 2025 that work totaled nearly $4 billion. He won the 2026 Democratic nomination for the seat.
issues: The campaign says that funding covered health care, infrastructure, agriculture, and education.
It also says the money covered broadband, public safety, clean water, and disaster recovery.
He presents that record as results on the issues that matter most in the district.
